issues.description: Sewer under Walker Street next to the Harvard/Radcliffe Quad is clogged and probably caved in since the street slopes down drastically toward the sidewalk.  The manhole cover on Walker street was pushed open by the water pressure during last night's rainstorm and half of Walker st. all the way across Shepard st. was flooded in the early morning hours.  The sewer not only needs to be unclogged, but probably sections of it need to be replaced since it is probably collapsed.
Drain is backed up and is causing flooding in stores. Please help.

issues.description:
The storm drains on woodside street are too small (and/or too few) to handle large volumes of rain.  On June 30th, a large rainstorm caused 2-3 feet of water to pool outside our home and flood the entire street - this water then rushed down our driveway and into the neighbor's yard, threatening to cause property damage.  I believe the neighbors said their basement did flood.

The way the street slopes towards North Street, along with water coming in from North Street, and the lack of additional/bigger storm drains leads to this situation whenever there is a large volume of rain... the storm on June 30th has been the worst in a while.  See image attached, which was taken on a lighter storm a few weeks ago, nowhere near as bad as June 30th.

Please note the drains are not clogged... once the
three fish fountain, in playground area, is stuck on, and one of the drains is clogged, so it is overflowing onto the playground.
